newsitem.title: CHINA: PRESS DIGEST - Chinese newspapers - March 13.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - Chinese newspapers - March 13.

text.p: Following is a summary of major Chinese political and business stories in leading newspapers, prepared by Reuters in Beijing. Reuters has not checked the stories and does not guarantee their accuracy. Telephone: (8610) 6532-1921. Fax: (8610) 6532-4978.

-- Li Ruihuan, who sits the Communist Party's seven-member decision-making standing committee and head of the advisory group to parliament the Chinese People's Political Consultative Conference, calls on the conference to help maintain national unity and stability.
- Minister of the State Family Planning Commission Peng Peiyun warns birth control workers not to rest on past successes or be blindly optimistic over population figures.
- Ping'an Insurance sets a profit target of 800 million yuan to 1.0 billion yuan and a premium income of 18-20 billion yuan in 1997.
- Shougang International Trading and Engineering Co, a unit of Capital Iron and Steel, makes an equity profit of 228 million yuan in 1996.
- The World Bank reduces its estimate of China's per capita GDP from $2,500 to $1,800.
- The State Council, or cabinet, orders rural cooperatives to boost loans to the farm sector, with at least 40 percent of loans going to agriculture.
- Silk authorities issue rules to regulate trading of silk cocoons, saying inter-provincial trading must be conducted through trading centres.
- The Erdos Group, holding company of B share listed Erdos Cashmere Products Co Ltd, reports pre-tax profits of 260 million yuan in 1996.
- China's motorcycle production is seen up 10 percent in 1997 to hit 7.5 million units. Motorcycle firms will face fierce competition as supply exceeds demand.
